recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. Revisit only if FHIR-I decides to reverse the FHIR-39137 structure and intentionally duplicate HTTP transport/header details on the search page again.
issue_request: FHIR-7891 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU1 FHIR-core request to clarify on the search-specific page what POST search URL servers should support and to include the HTTP-page guidance that resources returned in a Bundle do not have per-resource ETag or Last-Modified headers; the resolution was to update the page to make this clear.
initial_application: The issue was historically applied in git-svn commit 4f363ad0bd1afafaa97da59cb1cee0d469fcf2ef (svn r5534), which explicitly mentioned #7891 and added a POST [base]/[type]/_search example to source/search.html. That application did not duplicate the Bundle ETag/versionId sentence on search.html, and the surrounding source has since been materially refactored.
additional_context: Current source/search.html and source/http.html are active top-level pages linked from source/documentation.html. Later Published/Persuasive with Modification issue FHIR-39137 approved moving search transport protocol content from search.html to http.html, and commit e441170220c19e992f803667b245e63dcdd508cf implemented that structure. Current search.html describes search contexts and points readers to http.html#search for HTTP method details. Current http.html#search lists system, type, and compartment POST search endpoints, form-encoded body semantics, optional query-parameter handling, and marks search interaction versioning headers as N/A in the summary table. The general HTTP header section still states that Bundle-contained resources have no ETag and use resource meta.versionId directly. Direct Zulip and Confluence searches found no FHIR-7891-specific community evidence changing that conclusion.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current spec already provides the required POST URL clarification and authoritative header/versioning behavior, while duplicating that HTTP material back into search.html would conflict with the later FHIR-39137 page-structure decision and create maintenance drift.

related_jiras.note: Approved and applied the current structure that moves HTTP search method details from search.html to http.html while leaving a cross-reference from the search page.
